Module 1.title: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science
Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Electrochemistry
  • Nernst Equation: $E = E^0 - \frac{2.303 RT}{n F} \log Q = E^0 - \frac{0.0591}{n} \log Q$ at $298\,\text{K}$.
  • Electrochemical Corrosion: Anode oxidation ($M \to M^{n+} + n e^-$). Cathode reduction in acidic medium ($2H^+ + 2e^- \to H_2$) and neutral/alkaline aerated medium ($O_2 + 2H_2O + 4e^- \to 4OH^-$).
  • Corrosion Control: Sacrificial anode cathodic protection (Zn/Mg attached to steel), Impressed current cathodic protection, Galvanizing (Zn coating on Fe), Tinning.
Module 1.detailed_notes:
Module 1 Reference: Electrochemistry

Electrochemical series, reference electrodes (Calomel electrode, Glass electrode for pH measurement), and Pourbaix potential-pH diagrams.

Module 2.title: Spectroscopic Techniques and Analytical Chemistry
Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Spectroscopy
  • Beer-Lambert Law: $A = \log(I_0 / I) = \epsilon \cdot c \cdot l$, where $\epsilon$ is molar absorptivity.
  • UV-Visible Spectroscopy: Electronic transitions ($\sigma \to \sigma^*, n \to \pi^*, \pi \to \pi^*$). Chromophores and auxochromes.
  • IR Spectroscopy: Molecular vibrational modes (stretching and bending). Characteristic functional group frequencies ($-OH$ at $3200-3600\,\text{cm}^{-1}$, $>C=O$ at $1700\,\text{cm}^{-1}$).
  • NMR Spectroscopy: Proton chemical shift $\delta$ in ppm relative to TMS (tetramethylsilane).
Module 2.detailed_notes:
Module 2 Reference: Spectroscopy

Selection rules: UV-vis requires electronic dipole change; IR requires fluctuating dipole moment during vibration.
Module 2.textbook_html:
2.1 Molecular Spectroscopy and Chemical Characterization

Module 3.title: Polymer Chemistry, Nanomaterials and Composites
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Polymers & Nanomaterials
  • Classification: Thermoplastics (linear/branched, melt upon heating e.g. PE, PVC, PTFE) vs Thermosets (cross-linked 3D networks, decompose upon heating e.g. Bakelite, Epoxy).
  • Conducting Polymers: Conjugated $\pi$-electron backbones doped with charge carriers (e.g. polyaniline, polypyrrole).
  • Nanomaterials: Quantum confinement effects when dimensions $< 100\,\text{nm}$. Carbon nanotubes (CNT), Graphene (exceptional tensile strength $>100\,\text{GPa}$ and thermal conductivity).
Module 3.detailed_notes:
Module 3 Reference: Polymers

Glass transition temperature ($T_g$) marks transition from glassy brittle state to rubbery flexible state.

Module 4.title: Water Technology and Environmental Chemistry
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Water Treatment
  • Hardness of Water: Temporary ($Ca(HCO_3)_2, Mg(HCO_3)_2$, removed by boiling) vs Permanent ($CaCl_2, MgSO_4$, requires chemical softening). Expressed in ppm of $CaCO_3$ equivalent.
  • EDTA Titration: Hardness determined via complexometric titration using EDTA at pH 10 with Eriochrome Black-T (EBT) indicator (wine-red to blue end point).
  • Boiler Troubles: Scale and sludge formation, Priming and foaming, Caustic embrittlement ($NaOH$ attack at stressed boiler crevices).
  • Reverse Osmosis (RO): Applied hydraulic pressure exceeds osmotic pressure ($\Delta P > \Delta \pi$), driving pure water through semipermeable polyamide membrane.
Module 4.detailed_notes:
Module 4 Reference: Water Treatment

Demineralization using ion-exchange resin columns (cation exchanger $R-H$ and anion exchanger $R-OH$).

Module 5.title: Fuels, Combustion and Energy Storage Devices
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Fuels & Batteries
  • Calorific Value: Gross Calorific Value (HCV) vs Net Calorific Value (LCV): $LCV = HCV - 0.09 H \times 2442\,\text{kJ/kg}$.
  • Dulong's Formula: $HCV = \frac{1}{100}\left[ 33800 C + 144000\left(H - \frac{O}{8}\right) + 9270 S \right]\,\text{kJ/kg}$.
  • Knocking & Octane/Cetane Ratings: Petrol: Octane Number (isooctane = 100, n-heptane = 0). Diesel: Cetane Number (cetane = 100, $\alpha$-methylnaphthalene = 0).
  • Lithium-ion Batteries: Cathode: $LiCoO_2$, Anode: Graphite ($Li_x C_6$), Electrolyte: $LiPF_6$ in organic carbonates. High energy density ($>250\,\text{Wh/kg}$).
